meanings.note: Usually preceded by يوم (day) or definite الأحد in Jordanian schedules.

examples.text: يوم الأحد الصبح بنفتح المكتبة بدري.
examples.trans: On Sunday morning we open the library early.

examples.text: رح نتجمع كلنا بالحديقة يوم أحد هادي.
examples.trans: We will all gather in the park on a quiet Sunday.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: The color blue.

examples.trans: The color of my car is blue.

examples.text: السما اليوم لونها أزرق صافي وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky today is a clear blue and there are no clouds.

meanings.note: Refers both to physical foundations and to the base of a recipe or argument.

examples.text: أساس الكيكة لازم يكون خفيف ومستوي منيح.
examples.trans: The base of the cake needs to be light and baked well.

examples.text: الثقة هي أساس كل شغلنا بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: Trust is the foundation of all our work in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun for 'we' (equivalent to formal نحن).

examples.trans: We respect all our guests.
We are ready for breakfast.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of Form VIII اختبر; covers taste tests, school exams, and trials.

examples.text: عملنا اختبار للكيكات قبل ما نقدمهم للضيوف.
examples.trans: We ran a test on the cakes before serving them to guests.

examples.text: عندهم اختبار عربي بكرة الصبح بالمدرسة.
examples.trans: They have an Arabic exam tomorrow morning at school.

meanings.note: Form VIII verb taking a direct object.

examples.text: لازم نختبر حرارة الفرن قبل ما ندخل الصينية.
examples.trans: We need to test the oven temperature before putting the tin in.

examples.text: مازن بختبر كل وصفة بدقة كبيرة.
examples.trans: Mazen tests every recipe with great precision.

meanings.note: Command to a female to read.

examples.trans: Read the lesson out loud.

examples.text: اقرأي البطاقة بصوت عالي عشان كلنا نسمع.
examples.trans: Read the card out loud so all of us can hear.

meanings.note: Commonly refers to mulberries, which are popular in Jordan, or any berry.

examples.trans: Mulberry juice is very delicious in the summer.

examples.text: شجرة التوت بالحديقة صارت مليانة حبات سودة حلوة.
examples.trans: The mulberry tree in the garden is full of sweet dark berries now.

meanings.note: The staple food in Jordan, often a symbol of livelihood.

examples.trans: I bought the bread from the bakery in the morning.

examples.text: ريحة الخبز السخن طالعة من الفرن على الشارع.
examples.trans: The smell of warm bread is wafting out of the bakery onto the street.

meanings.note: The day of the week, Saturday.

examples.trans: Our weekend is on Saturday.

examples.text: يوم السبت الصبح دايماً بنروح نجيب خضرة من السوق.
examples.trans: On Saturday morning we always go buy vegetables from the market.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: The man who I saw yesterday.

examples.text: هذا المحل اللي اشترينا منه الكنافة الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: This is the shop where we bought the kunafa last week.

meanings.note: Form VII colloquial passive of باع (to sell).

examples.text: العسل البلدي بنباع بسوق السبت الصبح.
examples.trans: Local honey is sold at the Saturday morning market.

examples.text: كل الكتب المستعملة انباعت خلال ساعة.
examples.trans: All the second-hand books were sold within an hour.

meanings.note: Signature Jordanian/Palestinian pronunciation (with z) of بالضبط ('exactly!').

examples.trans: Exactly! You have become one of us.
Tell me exactly what to buy.

meanings.note: Both academic/historical research and physical searching.

examples.text: هادا البحث التاريخي أخد منا وقت طويل.
examples.trans: This historical research took us a long time.

examples.text: بعد بحث طويل لقينا الكرت جوا الكتاب.
examples.trans: After a long search we found the card inside the book.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

بشكل.gloss: in a way / in a shape

meanings.en: in a way / in a shape
meanings.note: Often used as a prefix for adverbs, e.g., 'bi-shakil ʿām' (generally).

examples.trans: We need to work in a faster way.
The ingredients are mixed in a completely even way.

meanings.note: Preposition 'between, among'.

examples.trans: Today you are mending things between two brothers!
The table is between the window and the door.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from تاريخ (history), agreeing with الساحة.

examples.text: وسط البلد فيه مباني تاريخية عمرها أكتر من مية سنة.
examples.trans: Downtown has historic buildings that are over a hundred years old.

examples.text: المدرج الروماني معلم تاريخي مهم بعمان.
examples.trans: The Roman Theater is an important historic landmark in Amman.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian and Levantine word used as a possessive marker, similar to "of" or "'s".

examples.trans: My brother's car is broken.
Where is the key belonging to the kitchen cupboard?

meanings.note: Levantine relational adjective formed from تحت ('under/below') + -aani; opposite of فوقاني.

examples.trans: The tuning wrench is in the bottom drawer.

examples.text: نور مسحت الألواح التحتانية للشباك الكبير.
examples.trans: Nour wiped the lower panes of the tall window.

meanings.note: Plural تعليمات (f. pl.) means instructions.

examples.trans: Follow the baking instructions written on the card.
The teaching at this school is very good.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Count to ten: one, two, three.

examples.text: رتبنا الصحون واحد تنين تلاتة عالطاولة.
examples.trans: We lined up the plates one, two, three on the table.

meanings.note: Noun of instance (ism marra) from لطّخ (to smudge).

examples.text: في تلطيخة حبر أزرق عالسطر التحتاني.
examples.trans: There is a blue ink smudge on the bottom line.
The smear of honey on the table sticks to your hand.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of لمّع ('to polish wood, brass, or shoes').

examples.text: بقي بس تلميع دواسات النحاس بقماشة ناعمة.
examples.trans: All that's left is polishing the brass pedals with a soft cloth.

examples.text: بعد التلميع رجع خشب الجوز يلمع زي المراية.
examples.trans: After polishing, the walnut wood shone like a mirror again.

meanings.note: Commonly used preposition for indicating proximity, next to, or beside.

examples.trans: Sit next to your brother.
We set the trays next to the fountain in the shade.

meanings.note: Standard Arabic and colloquial term for ink used in pens.

examples.trans: The pen ran out of ink.

examples.text: الحبر الأزرق نشف بسرعة عالورق السميك.
examples.trans: The blue ink dried quickly on the thick paper.

meanings.note: Standard and Jordanian feminine noun for a public park or walled garden (حدائق 'parks').

examples.trans: The park bench is painted beside the arch.

examples.text: بنتمشى بالحديقة كل يوم جمعة العصر.
examples.trans: We walk in the park every Friday afternoon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخاف, بيخاف).

examples.text: مازن خاف طول الليل من التقييم!
examples.trans: Mazen worried all night about the review!
I was afraid your stubborn brother would stay home.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: خبزات.

examples.trans: The morning bread is fresh and hot.
We ate bread with cheese and olives.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بخبط, بيخبط).

examples.text: شوي شوي عاللفة، لا تخبطوا الحيط!
examples.trans: Easy on the turn, do not bump the wall!
The wind rattled the window at night.

meanings.note: Used in cooking for cake batter and in general for any mix.

examples.text: اطوي التوت شوي شوي جوا خليط اللوز.
examples.trans: Fold the berries gently into the almond batter.

examples.text: هادا الخليط فيه عسل وبرش برتقال.
examples.trans: This mixture has honey and grated orange zest.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The weather today is very warm.

examples.text: الحليب الدافي بسكر الخميرة وبخليها تتفاعل.
examples.trans: Warm milk activates the yeast and helps it rise.

meanings.note: Form I verb; used both physically and for backing an idea.

examples.text: هادا هو البحث اللي انا بدعمه بقوة!
examples.trans: That is the research that I strongly support!

examples.text: كل الجيران دعموا فكرة مهرجان الحارة.
examples.trans: All the neighbours supported the idea of the neighbourhood festival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from ذهب (gold); also pronounced دهبي in everyday Jordanian.

examples.text: اخبزي الكيكة ليصير لونها ذهبي حلو.
examples.trans: Bake the cake until its colour turns a lovely golden.
She won a gold medal in the cooking competition.

meanings.note: Future tense marker in Jordanian and Levantine Arabic, equivalent to 'sa-' in MSA.

examples.trans: I will travel tomorrow.

examples.text: رح نذوق التلات كيكات بعد ما يبردوا شوي.
examples.trans: We will taste the three cakes after they cool a little.

meanings.note: Form I verb; can take عيون/عينيكي as object.

examples.text: ليش رمشتي عينيكي لما شفتي السطر التحتاني؟
examples.trans: Why did you squint your eyes when you saw the bottom line?

examples.text: ما رمش عينه وهو براقب الساعة.
examples.trans: He did not blink an eye while watching the clock.

meanings.note: Used frequently as an appreciative exclamation ('Wonderful!').

examples.text: روعة! الكيكة طلعت أطيب مما توقعنا.
examples.trans: Wonderful! The cake turned out even better than we expected.
Their carpentry work has precision and beauty.

meanings.note: Pull a door, a drawer or a heavy thing; also to withdraw money from a bank.

examples.trans: Pull the door towards you, don't push it.
I took money out of the bank this morning.

meanings.note: From سر, a secret. A secret room is غرفة سرية.

examples.trans: I have a secret plan for the holiday.

examples.text: هاد الرقم سري، لا تحكيه لحدا.
examples.trans: This number is secret, do not tell anyone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سطور.

examples.trans: Read me the top line of the letter.
He wrote two short lines on the card.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسواق.

examples.text: سوق وسط البلد مليان حركة الصبح.
examples.trans: The downtown market is bustling in the morning.
We bought fresh herbs from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: I like to drink tea after lunch.

examples.text: صبينا كاسات شاي ساخن مع ورق النعناع.
examples.trans: We poured glasses of hot tea with mint leaves.

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.text: امشي شوي شوي عشان ما توقع.
examples.trans: Walk slowly so you don't fall.

examples.text: استنوا شوي عشان تبرد الصواني تماما.
examples.trans: Wait a little so the trays cool down completely.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.text: عندي أخ صغير عمره خمس سنين.
examples.trans: I have a young brother who is five years old.

examples.text: في مفتاح نحاس صغير مخبي تحت الورقة.
examples.trans: There is a small brass key hidden under the sheet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أصوات.

examples.trans: I heard the sound of rain on the window.
His voice is calm and polite on the phone.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Used for a coat of paint (طبقة دهان), a layer of pastry, or a building storey.

examples.text: الطبقة الأولى نشفت وصارت جاهزة للطبقة التانية.
examples.trans: The first coat has dried and is ready for the second coat.

examples.text: دهان المي بيكفيه طبقتين رقيقتين عشان يطلع ناعم.
examples.trans: Water-based paint only needs two thin coats to come out smooth.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أطراف.

examples.trans: Pull the edge of the sheet tight.

examples.text: حط الكاسة بعيد عن طرف الطاولة.
examples.trans: Set the glass away from the edge of the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Can mean physically high or loud (for a voice or sound).

examples.trans: The music volume is very high.

examples.text: الرف العالي بالخزانة عليه كتب جدتي.
examples.trans: The high shelf in the cupboard holds my grandmother's books.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعرف, بيعرف).

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting in two seconds!
Do you know anyone here in Amman?

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: I went to the doctor because I am sick.

examples.text: استعملنا ورق نشافة عشان الحبر ما يطبع.
examples.trans: We used blotting paper so the ink would not stain.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: حطينا الخريطة على الطاولة وبلشنا نحللها.
examples.trans: We laid the map on the table and began analysing it.

meanings.note: Feminine noun; also used in the delighted Jordanian exclamation يا عيني! ('oh my! / how lovely!').

examples.trans: Close your eyes and smell the coffee!
Oh my, look at that warm light in the courtyard!

meanings.note: Leafy branch of a tree or climbing shrub.

examples.text: رفعنا الغصن الأخضر عن شنكل الشباك بلطف.
examples.trans: We gently lifted the green branch off the window latch.

examples.text: عصفور صغير وقف على غصن شجرة الليمون.
examples.trans: A little bird perched on a branch of the lemon tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: فناجين.

examples.trans: I set two teacups on the tray.
This is my favourite coffee cup.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: فوقانية, plural: فوقانيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.
The red ribbon is in the top pocket.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There are many people in the market.

examples.text: في تلات بطاقات ملونة جوا الظرف الكبير.
examples.trans: There are three coloured cards inside the big envelope.

meanings.note: Noun of unity from قطر; used both for liquid drops in recipes and eye/nose drops.

examples.text: زدنا قطرة مي زهر على الكريمة.
examples.trans: We added a drop of orange-blossom water to the cream.

examples.text: ما ضل ولا قطرة عسل بقاع المرطبان.
examples.trans: Not a single drop of honey was left at the bottom of the jar.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Refers to a pill in medical contexts or sometimes a coffee capsule.

examples.text: لازم توخذ كبسولة وحدة كل يوم.
examples.trans: You must take one capsule every day.

examples.text: البذور الصغيرة محفوظة جوا كبسولة شفافة عشان الرطوبة.
examples.trans: The tiny seeds are preserved inside a clear capsule against humidity.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كبيرة, plural: كبار).

examples.trans: We use this big paper ledger.
You know older brothers well!

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Placed AFTER the adjective or verb it intensifies: تقيلة كتير ('very heavy'), شكرا كتير ('thank you very much').

examples.trans: The smell is so good!
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; كرت بريد means 'postcard'. Plural: كروت.

examples.text: بعتتله كرت بريد قصير الأسبوع الماضي.
examples.trans: I sent him a short postcard last week.
I recognised his neat handwriting on the card right away.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from كريمة (cream); describes smooth dairy textures or off-white/cream hues.

examples.text: لون الحشوة كريمي ناعم وبدوب بالتم.
examples.trans: The filling is creamy, smooth, and melts in the mouth.

examples.text: اشترينا ورق رسم لونه كريمي دافي.
examples.trans: We bought drawing paper in a warm cream colour.

meanings.note: Names the heel of a foot or shoe (كعب القدم / كعب الحذاء).

examples.text: زحلق كعب حذائي عن حرف الطبلية الواطية.
examples.trans: The heel of my shoe slipped off the edge of the low stool.

examples.text: اسندي كعبك عالوسادة الطرية عشان ترتاح رجلك.
examples.trans: Rest your heel on the soft cushion so your foot can relax.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: All people love summer.

examples.text: كل بطاقة بالعلبة بتحكي عن نبتة عطرية مختلفة.
examples.trans: Every card in the tin talks about a different aromatic plant.

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.trans: I made a delicious chocolate cake.

examples.text: كيكة التوت اللي عملتها سلمى طلعت خفيفة وهشة.
examples.trans: The berry cake that Salma made turned out light and fluffy.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'no' or 'not', used exactly like Standard Arabic.

examples.trans: No, I don't want to go today.

examples.text: لا تنسوا تطفيوا الفرن بعد ما تخلصوا الخبيز.
examples.trans: Do not forget to turn off the oven after you finish baking.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.trans: The situation is perfect, don't worry.

examples.text: زينت سلمى وش الكيكة بشرايح لوز محمص.
examples.trans: Salma decorated the top of the cake with toasted almond slices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ألوان.

examples.trans: The colour of the suitcase is dark blue.
The courtyard colours are soothing to the eye.

meanings.note: The standard colloquial interrogative for 'why' in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Why were you late to work today?

examples.text: ليش الحبر على طرف الورقة مبين أغمق من النص؟
examples.trans: Why does the ink at the edge of the sheet look darker than the middle?

meanings.note: Collective noun denoting fibrous plant material or scrubbing sponge; unit noun is ليفة.

examples.trans: The box is wrapped in coarse palm-fibre twine.
Whole wheat is rich in natural fibres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبينة, plural: مبينين).

examples.trans: The wooden train looks old and precious.
It looks like it is going to rain tonight.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine form of مثل ('like, similar to').

examples.trans: Its color is dark blue like your suitcase!
The water is cold as ice.

meanings.note: Passive participle indicating that an object has been set down or positioned somewhere.

examples.trans: The key is placed on the table.

examples.text: المرطبان الدهبي محطوط على أعلى رف بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: The golden jar is placed on the highest shelf in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: مديرة). Plural: مدراء.

examples.trans: She became the permanent front-desk manager at the guesthouse.
The manager welcomed the new guests.

meanings.note: Used for flat surfaces like roofs or fields.

examples.trans: The roof of the house is flat.

examples.text: فردنا العجينة على لوح خشب مسطح ونضيف.
examples.trans: We rolled the dough out on a clean, flat wooden board.

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: I am not upset with you.

examples.text: هادا المفتاح مش للباب الرئيسي، هادا للخزانة.
examples.trans: This key is not for the main door; this one is for the cupboard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: مطابخ.

examples.trans: The smell of bread is coming from the kitchen.
The guesthouse kitchen is spacious and clean.

meanings.note: Standard word for rain, commonly used across all registers of Arabic.

examples.trans: There is a lot of rain outside.

examples.text: نزل مطر خفيف وغسل أوراق الياسمين بالساحة.
examples.trans: Light rain fell and washed the jasmine leaves in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from معدن (metal, mineral); describes metal containers as well as mineral water.

examples.text: البطاقات محفوظة جوا علبة معدنية صغيرة.
examples.trans: The cards are kept inside a small metal tin.

examples.text: أعطتنا قزازة مي معدنية باردة بعد المشي.
examples.trans: She gave us a cold bottle of mineral water after the walk.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine metathesis of ملعقة ('spoon'), placing the ع before the ل.

examples.text: حطّي معلقة صغيرة قرفة على وجه السحلب.
examples.trans: Put a teaspoon of cinnamon on top of the sahlab.

examples.text: نسيت أجيب المعلقة عشان أحرك الشاي فيها.
examples.trans: I forgot to bring the spoon to stir the tea with.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مكسورة, plural: مكسورين).

examples.trans: Put the broken valve in your coat pocket.
We fixed the broken chair leg.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of كوّن used as a noun; plural مكونات (ingredients).

examples.text: العسل البلدي هو أهم مكون بهاي الكيكة.
examples.trans: Local honey is the most important ingredient in this cake.

examples.text: قارنوا قائمة المكونات على الكرت التاني.
examples.trans: Compare the list of ingredients on the second card.

meanings.note: Popular aromatic herb in Jordanian tea traditions, prized for its gentle citrus scent.

examples.text: نقعنا أوراق مليسة طازجة مع الشاي الأخضر.
examples.trans: We steeped fresh lemon balm leaves with green tea.

examples.text: ريحة المليسة بالحديقة بتشبه قشر الليمون.
examples.trans: The scent of lemon balm in the garden resembles lemon zest.

meanings.note: Levantine passive participle of مزع ('to tear/rip'): feminine ممزوعة, plural ممزوعين.

examples.text: الورقة ممزوعة من الطرف، لازم نبدلها.
examples.trans: The sheet is torn at the edge, we need to replace it.

examples.text: كمّ القميص كان ممزوع من الشغل.
examples.trans: The shirt sleeve was torn from working.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am from Jordan.

examples.text: جبنا العسل البلدي الصافي من مزرعة قريبة.
examples.trans: We brought the pure local honey from a nearby farm.

meanings.note: Can refer to objects lacking moisture or metaphorically to a rude or blunt person.

examples.trans: The bread is dry, it can't be eaten.

examples.text: لازم نمسح الصحن بمنديل ناشف قبل ما نحط الكيكة.
examples.trans: We must wipe the plate with a dry cloth before putting the cake on.

meanings.en: to copy; trace a drawing; transcribe text
meanings.note: Form I verb (بنسخ / نسخ) used both for hand-copying drawings and copying text or files.

examples.text: نسخت الرسمة القديمة على ورقة نظيفة.
examples.trans: I copied the old drawing onto a clean sheet.

examples.text: ممكن تنسخ لي الوصفة على دفتري؟
examples.trans: Could you copy the recipe into my notebook for me?

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: The time is five and a half (half past five).

examples.text: التقينا بالساحة الساعة تمانية ونص تماما.
examples.trans: We met in the courtyard at eight-thirty sharp.

meanings.note: Plural noun with first person singular suffix.

examples.trans: My glasses broke yesterday.
I forgot my glasses next to the cup on the balcony.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for clean or tidy.

examples.trans: The house is clean after the deep cleaning.

examples.text: لوح الرخام نظيف وجاهز عشان نفرد عليه العجينة.
examples.trans: The marble slab is clean and ready for us to roll out the dough on.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian pronunciation (often نعنع in rapid speech) for fresh or dried mint added to tea.

examples.text: قطفنا شوية نعناع أخضر عشان الشاي.
examples.trans: We picked some fresh mint for the tea.
The dried mint in the jar has a strong aroma.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: This boy is very smart.

examples.text: هاد المحل ببيع أطيب كنافة نابلسية بعمان.
examples.trans: This shop sells the best Nabulsi kunafa in Amman.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian plural demonstrative ('these / those') for people or things.

examples.trans: Whose are these brass keys?
I have grown fond of those two rings!

meanings.note: Third person masculine pronoun.

examples.trans: He is the one who said so.

examples.text: طارق هو اللي اقترح نطلع رحلة على البترا.
examples.trans: Tareq is the one who suggested we take a trip to Petra.

meanings.note: Extremely common adverb used to express similarity or concluding a statement.

examples.text: هيك الحياة، يوم الك ويوم عليك.
examples.trans: Such is life, one day for you and one day against you.

examples.text: ما تحكي معه هيك قدام الناس، احكي معه على جنب.
examples.trans: Don't talk to him like that in front of people; speak to him privately.

meanings.note: Collective noun used for paper material or leaves of a tree.

examples.text: جيب لي شوية ورق أكتب عليهم.
examples.trans: Bring me some paper to write on.

examples.text: لفينا ورق دوالي اليوم الصبح للغدا مع اللبن.
examples.trans: We rolled grape leaves this morning for lunch with yogurt.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Oh Ahmed, come here.

examples.text: يا سيدي، تفضل اشرب معنا فنجان قهوة قبل ما تروح.
examples.trans: Sir, please come have a cup of coffee with us before you leave.

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today is a long day.

examples.text: سافرنا عالعقبة وقعدنا هناك يوم كامل عالشط.
examples.trans: We traveled to Aqaba and spent a whole day there at the beach.
